cards.q: What is a phonon?
cards.a: A quasiparticle of vibrational energy that uniformly oscillates at a single frequency in a medium.

cards.q: Phonons can be thought of as what kind of quantized waves?
Unlike photons, phonons are vibrations in what?
In an elastic structure, a phonon corresponds to what kind of state?
cards.a: An excited state in the modes of vibration.

cards.q: The study of phonons is an important part of which field of physics?
Which two conductivities of condensed matter systems do phonons play a major role in?
In solids with more than one atom in the smallest unit cell, which two qualities do phonons exhibit?
For optically trapped objects, when can a quantized vibration mode be defined as a phonon?
cards.a: As long as the modal wavelength of the oscillation is smaller than the size of the object.

cards.q: Who introduced the concept of phonons?
In what year was the concept of phonons introduced?
Who suggested the name "phonon"?
What does the Greek word φωνή (phonē), from which "phonon" comes, translate to?
What do long-wavelength phonons give rise to?
The name phonon emphasises an analogy to which other particle?
cards.a: The photon: phonons represent wave–particle duality for sound waves as photons do for light waves.

cards.q: In the lattice-dynamics treatment, what kind of lattice is assumed?
cards.a: A rigid, regular crystalline (not amorphous) lattice composed of N particles, which may be atoms or molecules.

cards.q: For a typical sample of a solid, the number of lattice particles N is of the order of what?
Why must atoms in a rigid lattice exert forces on one another?
cards.a: To keep each atom near its equilibrium position.

cards.q: Van der Waals forces, covalent bonds and electrostatic attractions in a lattice are ultimately due to which force?
Which forces between lattice atoms are generally negligible?
What does the pairwise potential energy function V of two lattice atoms depend on?
cards.a: The distance of separation of the atoms.

cards.q: Why is the sum of all pairwise potential energies multiplied by a factor of 1/2 for the entire lattice?
Why is summing the lattice potential only over neighboring atoms valid, even though electric forces extend to infinity?
cards.a: Because the fields produced by distant atoms are effectively screened.

cards.q: Under what condition may the lattice potentials V be treated as harmonic?
cards.a: As long as the atoms remain close to their equilibrium positions.

cards.q: How may the lattice resulting from the harmonic approximation be visualized?
cards.a: As a system of balls connected by springs.
